To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EDs have a negative impact on HRQOL and PD and, in turn, that poor HRQOL and high levels of PD are associated with the development and maintenance of EDs.
ED symptoms predicted reduced QoL and greater psychological distress, and that poor QoL and psychological distress in turn predicted increased ED symptoms.
EDs have a negative impact on QoL (both HRQoL, which was the main focus of our research, and PD) and that QoL (particularly PD) has a negative impact on ED symptoms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact that eating disorders (ED) have on quality of life (QL) and psychological distress, and the reciprocal impact that QL and distress have on the development of ED symptoms.
the bidirectional relationship between EDs and HRQoL, with the goal of informing the development of more effective and comprehensive treatments for EDs.
the reciprocal relationship between ED symptoms and HRQoL, and the impact that ED symptoms have on HRQoQL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ED symptoms, poor HRQo, and PD are all interrelated, and each has an influence on the others.
the bidirectional relationships between HRQoL, PD and ED symptoms are stable over time.
ED symptoms predict poor QoL and that poor QoL in turn predicts ED symptoms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
QoL and eating disorder symptoms are inextricably linked, with each influencing the other.
the relationship between EDs and QoL is bidirectional.
the bidirectional relationship between QoL and ED symptoms is complex, with both short and long term effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EDs are not just about symptoms, they also impact on other important areas of a person's life.
EDs and QoL have reciprocal relationships, and this needs to be taken into account when developing interventions for people with EDs.
QoL is a key target in the treatment of eating disorders.
